s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion in a patient with a history of ovarian cancer and chemotherapy
salient_findings: Elevated Krebs von den Lungen-6 level
Diffuse ground-glass opacity on chest CT
Lymphocytic predominance in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid
key_facts: Diagnosed with stage IV ovarian serous adenocarcinoma 7 years prior
Received TC chemotherapy followed by surgery
Krebs von den Lungen-6 level: 1250 U/mL
Autoantibodies related to connective tissue disease: negative
Total cell count in bronchoalveolar lavage: 615 cells/µL
Diffuse ground-glass opacity on chest CT 15 weeks after initial treatment
Mosaic attenuation and ill-defined centrilobular nodules on chest CT 15 weeks after second treatment

salient_findings: Elevated Krebs von den Lungen-6 level
Diffuse ground-glass opacity on chest CT
Lymphocytic predominance in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid

Received TC chemotherapy followed by surgery

differentials: Thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis with thymic carcinoma
Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia with underlying lymphoma
per_call: Thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis with thymic carcinoma
Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia with underlying lymphoma

shortlist.label: Chemotherapy-induced pulmonary fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of chemotherapy and symptoms of dyspnea on exertion

shortlist.label: Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated lymphocyte count in bronchoalveolar lavage and history of ovarian cancer

shortlist.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse ground-glass opacity on chest CT and symptoms of dyspnea on exertion

shortlist.label: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Bronchoalveolar lavage findings and history of ovarian cancer

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated eosinophil count in bronchoalveolar lavage and symptoms of dyspnea on exertion

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of dyspnea on exertion, elevated Krebs von den Lungen-6 level, and chest CT findings of diffuse ground-glass opacity, mosaic attenuation, and ill-defined centrilobular nodules are consistent with nonspecific interstitial pneumonia, particularly in the context of her history of chemotherapy for ovarian cancer.

rejected.label: Chemotherapy-induced pulmonary fibrosis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of chemotherapy, the presence of ground-glass opacity and lack of honeycombing on chest CT make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient's bronchoalveolar lavage showed a high percentage of lymphocytes, but the clinical and radiological findings do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient's chest CT findings do not show the characteristic features of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, such as nodular opacities or a bronchial distribution.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient's bronchoalveolar lavage showed only 12% eosinophils, which is not sufficient to support a diagnosis of eosinophilic pneumonia.
